points: Q2 2026 results are already on the books from the August 4 release; the November 4 print will reveal whether data-center demand for EPYC and Instinct MI350/MI400 stayed strong through the September quarter, since that segment drove 2025 growth of $16.6 billion, up 32%.
The Q3 print will show if gross margin can hold or expand from the 50% level reported for 2025, despite the roughly $440 million in inventory and related charges that already affected the mix.
Q4 2026 guidance and any FY1/FY2 commentary will test the consensus expectation of 81% FY1 EPS growth and 105% FY2 growth; a reiteration or raise supports the long case.

Client and gaming demand after the summer quarter and any stabilization in embedded revenue will show whether the 2025 patterns — client/gaming up 51% and embedded down 3% — are improving or at least not dragging into Q4.

Updates on the AI GPU ramp, including MI400 and Helios, plus supply/demand commentary, will shape the setup for the next two to four months and provide a read-through ahead of SMCI’s November 9 print.
The valuation flag is fair versus the computer-industry theme, so the trade hinges on forward EPS acceleration — the consensus PEG of about 0.77 — rather than multiple expansion.
watch: Data-center revenue growth stays at or above the 2025 32% pace — supports the long.
Gross margin holds at or above 50% — supports the long.
FY1 EPS consensus moves higher from $7.57 or is not cut — supports the long.
Q4 guidance is raised or in-line with the 32-up/5-down analyst revision trend — supports the long.
